raw_response:
I've been farming these 42 mu for 40 years now, since I was fourteen. Never went to school — the land taught me everything I know. My old man farmed here before me, and his old man before that. I've got my wife, my son and daughter-in-law, and my little grandson in the house — five mouths to feed. The land is split into three parcels: the big flat field of 30 mu where I do wheat then maize, the south field of 10 mu for cotton, and the old greenhouse by the house where my daughter-in-law tends 2 mu of cucumber.

**Wheat (30 mu)** — I'm planting in mid-October, same as every year. I saved seed from last year's crop, but I bought some new seed too — the shop in town sells it for about 40 yuan per mu. Mixing saved and new seed works best; pure saved seed gets weak after too many years. Before planting, I spread one full bag of compound fertilizer per mu — the 50-jin bags, same as always. I don't know how many kilograms that is, I know bags. Then in March when the wheat greens up, if it looks yellow I topdress with half a bag of urea per mu. Last year I put more fertilizer on one plot and the wheat grew too tall, lodged flat in the wind — lost half that patch. This year I'm sticking to what I know: one bag compound, half bag urea. I'll irrigate three times — after planting if it's dry, once at green-up, and once at heading. The well water isn't free, the meter runs fast, but you can't skip it. I expect about 900 jin per mu if the weather holds, same as last year.

**Maize (30 mu, same land)** — Comes right after wheat in mid-June. The turnaround is tight — sometimes we cut wheat in the morning and plant maize the same afternoon. I always buy hybrid seed for maize, can't save it, doesn't work. Costs about 50 yuan per mu. One bag of compound fertilizer at planting, and I might topdress a bit of urea when it's knee-high if the leaves look pale. Irrigate maybe twice — once if it's dry at planting, and once at tasseling. Last year the maize did well, about 1000 jin per mu. Hope for the same. Harvest is late September, early October.

**Cotton (10 mu)** — Planting in mid-April on the south field. Cotton needs a lot of hand work. I buy seed from the shop, about 35 yuan per mu. Before planting I put down about three-quarters of a bag of compound fertilizer per mu, then some urea when it flowers. Irrigate twice — at flowering and when the bolls are filling. Pests are always trouble on cotton, so I spray insecticide when I see them, and herbicide once early. The real work is picking — three, sometimes four rounds from September to October. My wife and I can't do it all. I hire women from the village and sometimes from down south — pay them by the kilo picked. That's my biggest cash expense after fertilizer. I expect about 500 jin of seed cotton per mu.

**Cucumber (2 mu)** — In the greenhouse near the house. My daughter-in-law and my wife manage this. We buy new hybrid seed every year, about 150 yuan per mu — expensive, but greenhouse cucumber needs the good seed. Plant in early March under the plastic. We put in two cartloads of manure before planting, then two bags of compound fertilizer per mu split into two times, plus some urea and potassium fertilizer every couple weeks once the fruit sets. Water almost every few days when it's hot — six times or more through the season. Spray fungicide and insecticide when needed; damp greenhouse gets disease easy. It's the most work per mu, but the price at market is good. Expect about 7000 jin per mu.

Money is tight. I have to buy fertilizer for wheat, maize, and cotton all at once in spring, plus seed, plus diesel for the pump. I can't afford to experiment. I do what I did last year, what my neighbors do, what my father did. My neighbor Lao Wang tried some new slow-release fertilizer last year and said it was fine, but it cost more and I didn't see his wheat do any better than mine. I'm not changing. I'd rather waste a little money on slightly too much fertilizer than risk a bad year — a bad year means borrowing money, and I hate owing.
